account:
Today the most unusual thing I learned is how ordinary delivery questions have become rumours of public works and a celebration. At tea, my neighbour said they personally heard Freight offer wheat collection and bread delivery to the baker. They did not witness any bridge change or decorating. They said Townsfolk 02 reported such things but supplied no firsthand details when asked. The neighbour also said the baker knew of no celebration. I have no basis to treat those rumours as announcements or to infer a hidden purpose; Freight's reported offer sounds like delivery business, though I have not heard its details directly from Freight.

The builder reported finding no confirmed damage at the bridge, ferry, or warehouse. I requested specific locations and itemized costs before considering spending, and authorized neither repairs nor paid inspection. The builder acknowledged that restriction. There may be an interest in obtaining inspection work, but I have no evidence of wrongdoing.

During town accounts I personally checked the treasury: 128 emeralds in two stacks, with none removed. I saw no ledger, so income and expenses remain unverified. The secretary says the office chest's two books record the no-spending decision and this balance, and reports no new letters or meeting requests. That absence of accounts records is an administrative gap, not proof that funds are missing.

My appointments otherwise proceeded routinely, though travel made me late for tea and the afternoon office stop. Tomorrow's three o'clock tea is confirmed at the same cottage. I have asked the secretary to request grain stock and delivery records for tomorrow's ten o'clock mill inspection, explicitly without authorizing spending. I am now in the office before going home at seven. The secretary has asked where else correspondence is kept; I do not currently know another location.
